text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-gpu-7` p99 > 10s for 5m, queue_depth=970 (alert threshold 300), autoscaler_lag=85s. Streaming stalls observed. Affected customer: AcmeRetail. Pager -> @maria-sre oncall.

maria-sre: ack. looking at dashboards now. any recent deploys to dedicated pools?

raj-runtime: no runtime deploys in last 30m. seeing warmup failure rate ~35% on new nodes, KV cache misses spiking. raw logs snippet:```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] pool=dedicated-prod-gpu-7 warmup_state=failed handshake_timeout=45s node_id=gpu-12
[2026-03-15T14:02:34Z] queue_depth=872 p95=2.3s p99=12.1s streaming_stalls=74 rate_limit=0
```

kevin-platform: autoscaler issued scale-up at 14:01:30, handshake started 14:01:40 but node allocations stalled. infra shows image mount errors to NFS mirror (503). likely image pull / mount flakiness causing warmup to fail.

maria-sre: probable chain: warmup orchestration failing -> autoscaler keeps queuing requests -> backlog builds -> p99/streaming stalls. mitigation plan (short): 1) throttle non-critical tenants by route-tag, 2) attach fallback hotshot pool with small quantized model, 3) drain longest inflight requests, 4) increase handshake timeout temporarily. Who can flip routing?

raj-runtime: I can. running: `redwood route update --pool dedicated-prod-gpu-7 --throttle low-priority=50%` then `redwood pool attach --pool us-west-hotshot --model rwd-small-quant --temp true`. expect ~90s to start rerouting.

sophie-support: noting impact in support ticket SR-7653, pinging account lead for AcmeRetail. prepping initial customer note. @emily-pm please draft comms.

emily-pm: on it. will say degraded latency and streaming interruptions, ETA for update 30m. assigning account lead to coordinate.

raj-runtime: routing flips done. fallback pool attached. immediate metrics: queue_depth -> 420 in ~2m. p95 -> 1.1s. p99 still ~6.8s due to inflight streaming sessions.

maria-sre: draining long-running requests: `rq kill --older-than 120s --pool dedicated-prod-gpu-7` to reduce tail. bumped handshake timeout to 120s to allow warmup more time.

kevin-platform: infra note: NFS mirror returned transient 503s during image pulls at 14:00-14:03. applied hotfix to mount logic to retry/backoff. warmup success rate improving (65% -> 92% over 5m).

incident-bot: UPDATE: severity downgraded P1 -> P2. continue monitoring.

sophie-support: AcmeRetail confirms partial recovery; still seeing stalls for sessions established before 14:04. they requested a full postmortem. added details to SR-7653.

maria-sre: handing off active triage to @raj-runtime for next watch. summary for handoff: root cause likely NFS mount flakiness causing warmup failures and autoscaler lag -> pool saturation -> queue backlog -> streaming stalls/p99 breach. mitigations applied: route throttles, fallback pool attach, drained long requests, increased handshake timeout, infra hotfix for mount retries. current metrics: p95 ~1.0s, p99 ~2.8s, queue_depth ~120. will monitor 30m.

raj-runtime: taking over. follow-ups I'll own: - create GH issues for warmup idempotency/local fallback - autoscaler backoff/tuning to avoid pile-up - alerting: warmup_failure_rate earlier detection. postmortem owner: @kevin-platform. I'll file tickets and link.

maria-sre: thanks team. note for next oncall: consider lowering `warmup_failure_rate` alert threshold to 5% to detect faster. full handoff at 14:55 UTC.

emily-pm: drafted customer timeline and will post to #customer-comm for review.

-- end of thread --
